specialty: clarity: can a competent reader follow the claim chain? Are tables self-describing? Is any number ambiguous about its unit or denominator?
summary: The paper argues that a multiple-choice score should be tested against the construct's best constant, input-blind predictor (the 'floor') before any arm-to-arm comparison, and that this floor must itself be calibrated because it is a maximum over k noisy label marginals. It contributes: (i) a nine-construct floor-vs-chance table with the floor's own sampling distribution under a legality-aware balanced null (Table 1, p.14), showing only MMLU and BoolQ clear that null at p<1e-5 while six others sit at p=0.083-0.853; (ii) a demonstration that content-side floors are not dataset constants but functions of (dataset, tie convention, length unit, tokenizer), with a 40.6-point span on MMLU-Pro (Table 2, p.15); (iii) an MMLU-Pro-scale read-out over 17 designated damaged cells where 15/17 sit at or below the floor while most read above a chance line (Table 5, p.18), plus a symmetric-standard restatement that shrinks the flip to 3/12 vs 1/12 (Sec 5.1, p.7); (iv) an arm-conditional stratified permutation null (v2) that is exactly zero for any constant emitter and re-sorts a 27-cell read-out (Table 7, p.20). I recomputed the load-bearing arithmetic from the shipped evidence and it holds up: the nine floors are exact rationals (1403/12032, 3776/14042, 2033/3270, 138/500, 633/2376, 311/1172, 255/1221, 928/1838); the 0.299 pp ordering slack is exactly (1439-1403)/12032=0.29921 pp; '13 of the 27 clear the floor by more than 0.299 pp' is exactly 13 by my independent recount from Table 7's acc-hat column, with Llama-2 k12 the tightest at 0.0078 pp and 94.82% of its weight in A-argmax strata; the binomial P(X>=3 | n=12, p=.05)=0.01957; 2532/14042=18.032%; the residual-inflation ratios 2.11x/0.90x/0.98x reproduce from gate2 CSV columns (0.472574/0.223629=2.1132, 0.388149/0.430426=0.9018, 0.693617/0.708445=0.9791); always-A/E/J v1 deltas of 0.000/-2.111/-3.807 pp reproduce from the gold marginals. All 17 cited artifact paths exist. The paper is unusually honest about its own defects, including a self-inflicted null-support error on its flagship construct. My concerns are almost entirely about legibility of the claim chain, not soundness: the paper is a 26-page instrument with 12 tables and 0 figures, every table is in the appendix, and the main text has become a chain of hedges whose net claim a reader must assemble by hand. I also found two concrete numeric/definitional defects and one caption-vs-body contradiction, all fixable without new experiments.
strengths: The central protocol claim is clearly stated and correctly separated into two questions with different required dependence, and the separation is made legible by a purpose-built table. Table 3 (p.16) is the single best piece of exposition in the paper: two rows, columns 'Question' / 'Null' / 'Required dependence', giving v1=arm-independent and v2=arm-conditional. Sec 3.2 (p.4) then earns it by showing v1 is NOT collapse-invariant on the full MMLU-Pro item set (always-A/-E/-J get 0.000, -2.111, -3.807 pp for identical zero information). I verified those three deltas from evidence/mmlu_scale_power/mmlu_pro_power_nulls_v2.json:letter_null.gold_letter_marginal_frac: A=0.11660572, E=0.09549535, J=0.07854056, giving exactly 0.000/-2.111/-3.807 pp against the always-A floor. A reader who reads only Sec 3.2 plus Table 3 understands why one null cannot do both jobs.

The self-falsification in Appendix A.1.5 (pp.13-14) is exemplary and, unusually, is written so a reader can audit the direction of the correction rather than just the fact of it. The paragraph 'Which rows moved, and in which direction' names the case split (n_opt<k raises p and hurts the authors; n_opt>k lowers p and helps them), identifies which rows are in which case, and explicitly retracts a prior blanket claim that 'such a fix can only move against the authors'. This is confirmed verbatim in evidence/construct_nulls_legality_aware.json:directionality, which records the contradiction against the earlier MAIN record and lists n_rows_moving_in_authors_favour=2. I could not find any place where the paper absorbed a favourable movement silently.

Table 10 (p.23) is a genuinely self-describing generated artifact and it does something I rarely see: it keeps the superseded column next to the corrected one, so a reader can see the size and sign of the correction without re-running anything. The caption states the emitter path, sha256 (5ee8fa39d5fb), superseded sha256 (275112623d05), seed 20260814, n_draws 1e6, and the method string verbatim; and it explains the check that 'where n_opt is constant the two nulls are the same distribution and the columns agree by construction, which is itself a check on the emitter'. I verified this construction-check holds for MMLU/OpenBookQA/CommonsenseQA/BoolQ (agreement to 3 dp) -- see weakness 1 for the one row where it visibly does NOT hold and is not explained in the caption.

The paper holds both sides of its headline flip to one evidentiary standard and reports that this shrinks its own effect, in the main text rather than an appendix footnote. Sec 5.1 (p.7) prints the 2x2 (10/12 point-estimate vs 3/12 CI-excluding-zero for chance; 3/12 vs 1/12 for the floor) and then says in the body 'about a third of its advertised size'. The 12 per-cell CIs are all present in evidence/mmlu_scale_power/mmlu_pro_power_nulls_v2.json:crossfamily; the floor side's 1/12 (qwen3 k14, CI [0.0416, 0.4239]) and the two below-floor cells (llama2 k8, qwen3 k8) reproduce exactly. The follow-on qualification -- that under BH or Bonferroni neither reference retains a cell (0/12 both sides) so the comparison is 'undefined rather than 3/12 versus 1/12', with the surviving statement being the binomial count P(X>=3)=0.0196 -- is correct arithmetic (I recomputed 0.019568) and is exactly the right level of caution.

Denominators are defined once and the definition is enforced mechanically, and the paper names its own prior violation of that rule with the omitted cells and their values. Sec 4 'Designated damaged cells' (p.6) and Appendix A.4 (p.16) both state the set (5 OLMo-2 arms + 4 truncation rungs x 3 families = 17 MMLU-Pro cells, 17x5=85 off-MMLU, Winogrande excluded), and A.4 records that an earlier version counted only keep12/keep10/keep8 as OLMo-2 damaged, silently omitting shortgpt16 (+3.674, p=0.0001) and keep14 (+0.324, p=0.3234). evidence/construct_nulls_legality_aware.json:floor_invariance_verified.F3_per_family_damaged_rungs confirms the widened set, and its F3_note explains why that field is deliberately diagnostic-only rather than asserted against a literal. For a clarity reviewer this is the difference between a denominator I can check and one I have to trust.

The v2 statistic is correctly and repeatedly de-claimed, which removes the single largest novelty risk from the reader's path. Sec 3.2 (p.4) states 'Delta_perm is the numerator of Cohen's kappa evaluated within n_opt strata', gives the identity Delta_perm = kappa(1-pe), says the constant-emitter zero 'is the textbook property', and confines the contribution to (i) the stratification and (ii) the use as a gate. Appendix A.2 (p.15) then attributes option-count-aware chance correction result-by-result to Bennett 1954, Brennan & Prediger 1981, Frary 1988, Brenner & Kliebsch 1996, Vries 2008. A reader is never left guessing which part is claimed.
weaknesses: DEFECT 1 (numeric, PIQA row of Table 10, p.23) -- the generated manifest's two p columns are NOT comparable for PIQA, and the caption asserts they are. The caption says the two columns 'differ only in whether that null is realizable' and that 'where n_opt is constant the two nulls are the same distribution and the columns agree by construction'. PIQA's n_opt IS constant (evidence/construct_nulls_legality_aware.json rows[7].n_opt_is_constant=true, n_opt_hist={"2":1838}), yet the printed columns disagree: blind 0.658 vs legal 0.691. Reading the row gives a reader the false impression that legality changed PIQA's p by +3.3 pp. The evidence file is explicit that it did not: rows[7].p_change_attribution = 'threshold convention only (n_opt is constant, so the null is identical)', and rows[7].p_2x2 gives all four combinations: blind_rounded_floor__as_shipped=0.6576, blind_exact_floor=0.691985, aware_rounded_floor=0.657341, aware_exact_floor__primary=0.691229. The emitter prints p_blind_shipped (rounded-floor convention) in one column and p_aware (exact-floor convention) in the other, so the PIQA column difference is entirely the FLOOR-ROUNDING convention, a second and unrelated defect. Confirmed in code/emit_tab_construct_nulls.py:428 (blind column = fmt_p(r["p_blind_shipped"], ...)) with no convention-matching. The row that most needs the two-column contrast to be clean is instead the one that silently mixes two corrections. Fix without new experiments: print blind_exact_floor (0.692) in the blind column, or add a third column, or state the convention mismatch in the caption. Note the same mixing exists on the MMLU-Pro rows but is invisible there because blind rounds to 0.000 either way (p_blind_shipped=0.0 exact and rounded).

DEFECT 2 (numeric, Appendix A.1.5, p.14, 03b_nulls.tex:37) -- the two ARC directionality figures printed in the paper do not match the shipped evidence, and the mismatch is roughly 40%. The paper writes ARC-Easy and ARC-Challenge 'move slightly in our favour, by -0.0025 and -0.0063 in p --- real rather than Monte-Carlo error at roughly -17 and -23 standard errors'. The shipped record gives -0.004 and -0.005 (evidence/construct_nulls_legality_aware.json:directionality, top-level string), and the per-row measurements are dp_aware_minus_blind = -0.0012050 at dp_sigma = -3.339 (ARC-Easy, rows[4].directionality) and -0.0052133 at dp_sigma = -7.336 (ARC-Challenge, rows[5].directionality). None of -0.0025 / -0.0063 / -17 / -23 appears anywhere in the evidence directory (I grepped every .json/.csv/.tsv/.md under evidence/; the only hits for 0.0025 and 0.0063 are unrelated boot_p values in gate2_letter_content_nulls). All four numbers DO appear verbatim in code/recompute_legality_aware_nulls.py lines 77-78, in a docstring describing an earlier '8 seeds x 1e6 draws' run; the shipped record is 3 seeds x 2e5 draws (n_draws_per_seed=200000, seeds_checked=[20260814,7,99]). So the manuscript is quoting a superseded intermediate. The direction and the conclusion survive -- both rows still move in the authors' favour, both stay far from 0.05, and the bracket values 0.140->0.136 and 0.453->0.447 are correct -- but a sigma figure of -17 where the record says -3.34 is a 5x overstatement of how far the ARC-Easy shift is from Monte-Carlo error, in the paragraph whose whole purpose is to establish that these shifts are real rather than noise. This defect is invisible to the shipped prose checker: code/check_prose_vs_evidence.py:104 sets MIN_DP=3 and its targets are floors and chance lines only (build_targets adds only 'floor', 'chance', 'longest_split_char/token' quantities), so no directionality delta or sigma is in its target space at all. The Reproducibility Statement's '610 numerals with none unresolved' should therefore not be read as covering these.

DEFECT 3 (caption vs body contradiction, Table 5, p.18 vs Appendix A.8, p.18) -- Table 5's caption and the paragraph that introduces it disagree on how many cells the table contains, and the disagreement is exactly the denominator the paper spent Appendix A.4 fixing. The caption reads 'over all 17 designated damaged cells'; the introducing sentence in 09_appendix.tex:16-17 reads 'Table 5 is the MMLU-Pro letter read-out for all 12 cross-family cells'. Neither number is the row count: the table has 14 printed rows, because Llama-3's four rungs are collapsed into one range row ('k14--k8', 0.111868--0.114694). So a reader counting rows gets 14, the caption says 17, the pointer says 12, and the true content is 17 cells rendered as 14 rows. Given that the paper's most serious self-reported prior defect (A.4) was an undisclosed denominator narrowing, having the flagship per-cell table disagree with itself about 17-vs-12-vs-14 is the highest-value single fix in the paper. Fix: make the caption say '17 designated damaged cells in 14 rows; Llama-3's four rungs are collapsed into one range row', and change 09_appendix.tex to say 17.

The main text no longer stands alone: all 12 tables are after the bibliography, so every quantitative claim in Sections 3-5 is a forward reference across the reference list. Table 1 is cited on p.2 and printed on p.14; Table 3 cited p.4 printed p.16; Table 7 cited p.4, p.5 and p.8, printed p.20; Table 5 cited p.7, printed p.18. main.tex:25-33 and 39-44 document that this was a deliberate response to the 9-page limit, and I confirmed the main text ends at y=319 on p.10 with REFERENCES at y=346 (i.e. it still spills ~43% down page 10, so the relocation did not actually achieve the 9-page target it was performed for). The result is that the reader of Sec 5.1 is asked to accept '10/12 above chance, 1/12 above floor, 15/17 at or below floor' with no table in sight for eleven pages. A single small in-text table or figure for the headline 2x2 and the 17-cell summary would cost far less space than it recovers in legibility.

Zero figures in 26 pages, for a paper whose entire thesis is a comparison of reference lines. The claim 'a score can sit above chance and below its floor' is inherently one-dimensional and would be immediately legible as a single number line per construct with three marks (chance, floor, arm score) and the CI. Instead a reader must mentally align Table 1's Chance/Floor/E[f-hat]/q95 columns with Table 5's Accuracy/Delta columns across four pages. I checked every page for images and captions: 0 images, 0 'Figure N:' captions. For a measurement/protocol paper meant to change what people report, the absence of a single canonical picture of the reporting rule is a real adoption cost, not just an aesthetic one.

The word 'construct' -- the paper's central unit and the noun in every denominator -- is never defined, and it is used with at least three different scopes, which makes several counts unverifiable by a reader. Sec 3.1 (p.4) says 'For a letter construct with legal labels L' but never says what a construct is. Sec 4 (p.6) then says 'The target inventory comprises ten constructs plus the control', which requires counting (benchmark x interface) pairs, and immediately adds the disambiguating rule 'OpenBookQA content is reported under both character and token units rather than counted twice' -- i.e. the unit of counting is neither benchmark nor (benchmark, interface, unit). Meanwhile the abstract says 'eight letter constructs' and Table 1 has nine rows because MMLU-Pro appears twice (once per chance convention), so the nine-row table is eight constructs. A reader cannot reconstruct 'ten' or 'eight' from any stated rule. One sentence in Sec 3 defining construct = (benchmark, interface [, content specification]) plus one sentence enumerating the ten would close this.

Two of the paper's decision constants are asserted without any stated justification, which weakens the reporting rule it wants adopted. Sec 3.2 (p.5) requires 'at least 0.10 times the same-family intact anchor for a material signal' and blocks relative claims if the anchor itself is below 0.10; both 0.10s carry no rationale, and the second is a different quantity from the first (absolute recovery_fraction vs a ratio to the anchor). The consequences are load-bearing: qwen3 k14 is dismissed as immaterial at 9.1% of its anchor, and the entire Llama-2 family is blocked at anchor recovery_fraction=0.0545 (both verified in evidence/heal_readout_v2_permutation_null.json: cells[16].relative_recovery=0.09068, family_anchors.llama2_7b.recovery_fraction=0.05453, min_anchor_recovery=0.1). Sec 3.2 says the constant was pre-registered, which addresses gaming but not calibration -- a reader adopting the checklist has no basis for choosing 0.10 over 0.05 or 0.20, and 9.1% vs a 10% bar is close enough that the qualitative verdict flips under any nearby choice.

Sec 5.1 compresses six distinct claims into one paragraph with three different denominators (12, 17, 85) and two different chance definitions, and the reader must track which is which without a signpost. In the space of one page (p.7) the text moves through 10/12 and 12/12 above chance under two chance lines, 1/12 above floor, 4-of-5 OLMo-2, 15/17, then 3/12-vs-1/12 under the symmetric standard, then 9/85 and 45/85 off-MMLU, then 0/15 and 0/60 and 7/60 and 52/60. Each count is individually correct (I verified 15/17 and the 12-cell CI counts against the crossfamily records, and the off-MMLU nine are enumerated in A.6 as 5 shortgpt16 + 4 keep14), but no reader can hold seven denominators in working memory. Grouping them into a small table with columns (scope, n, above chance, above floor) would make the same content checkable at a glance.

Some captions cite evidence identifiers that resolve, through Table 12, to a document that is not in the released artifact, so a reader following a caption to its source can dead-end. Table 12 (p.26) maps E-A and E-K to 'tcodex_out/EVIDENCE_PACK.md, Section A / Section K'. That file is not present anywhere in the submission snapshot (I checked: no tcodex_out directory, no file matching EVIDENCE_PACK), and MANIFEST.json's cited_paths list does not include it, so the freeze gate's 'named_artifacts_missing: []' does not cover it. Table 11's caption cites E-K for the 16-row ledger; the machine-readable half of that map (evidence/claim_evidence_map.tsv) is present but has 16 rows numbered H-01..H-04 + C-01..C-16, i.e. 20 rows, so the caption's 'correspond one-to-one with the rows here' is a claim about a 16-of-20 subset that a reader has to work out. Separately, claim_evidence_map.tsv:C-13 still reads 'The honest MMLU-Pro count is 14/15' while Table 11 row 13 now reads 15/17 -- the denominator fix reached the manuscript but not the shipped map, and H-02/H-04 cite evidence/s2_03_symmetric_inference.json and evidence/s2_02_stratified_ordering.json, neither of which is in the snapshot.

The Limitations section (pp.9-10) is where a reader learns that the paper's originally planned causal contrast no longer exists, and this is not surfaced anywhere earlier. 'The planned causal contrast has dissolved' (p.10) reports that H_heal's antecedent required unhealed Qwen3 k8 to sit below an arm-conditional null and it does not (-0.139, p=0.0964), and that H_family is unavailable because 0/27 cells are significantly below the permutation null. Sec 6 (p.9) mentions 'A healed non-OLMo arm is in training, but it is not part of this paper's evidence' in a way that reads as forward-looking rather than as a dissolution. A reader who stops at Sec 6 will not know that two of the study's designed contrasts are structurally unavailable, not merely unmeasured. One sentence in the introduction's contribution list would fix this and would cost the paper nothing, since the surviving claim is independent of both.
questions: Table 10 PIQA row: can you confirm the blind column is p_blind_shipped (rounded-floor threshold) while the legal column is p_aware (exact-floor threshold), so that PIQA's 0.658 vs 0.691 is the rounding convention and not legality? If so, will you print p_2x2.blind_exact_floor (0.692) instead, or add the convention as a column, so that the row stops contradicting the caption's 'agree by construction' claim for constant-n_opt rows?

Appendix A.1.5: what is the provenance of '-0.0025 and -0.0063 in p' and 'roughly -17 and -23 standard errors'? The shipped record gives dp = -0.0012050 (sigma -3.34) for ARC-Easy and -0.0052133 (sigma -7.34) for ARC-Challenge over 3 seeds x 2e5 draws, and the paper's four numbers appear only in a docstring in code/recompute_legality_aware_nulls.py:77-78 describing an 8-seed x 1e6-draw run. Was that earlier run persisted anywhere, or should the sentence be re-emitted from the shipped record?

Table 5: is it 17 cells or 12? The caption says 17, 09_appendix.tex says 12, and 14 rows are printed because Llama-3's four rungs are one range row. Which count is the table, and will the caption state the row-collapse explicitly?

What exactly is a 'construct'? A one-sentence definition plus an enumeration of the ten would let a reader verify 'ten target constructs', 'eight letter constructs', and Table 1's nine rows against each other. As written I can reconstruct none of the three from a stated rule.

Where does the 0.10 materiality constant come from, and is the same 0.10 doing two different jobs (a fraction of the anchor for a cell, and an absolute recovery_fraction floor for the anchor)? Since qwen3 k14 lands at 9.1% of its anchor, the immateriality verdict flips under any nearby constant; what would a reader adopting the checklist use to pick it?

Would you consider one small main-text table (scope, n, above chance, above floor) covering the 12 / 17 / 85 denominators, and one number-line figure for a single construct showing chance, floor, q95 of the floor estimator, and an arm score with its CI? Both are zero-new-experiment additions and would make the headline checkable without the eleven-page forward reference to Table 1.

Is tcodex_out/EVIDENCE_PACK.md intended to be part of the released artifact? Table 12 maps E-A and E-K to it and it is absent from the snapshot; likewise evidence/s2_02_stratified_ordering.json and evidence/s2_03_symmetric_inference.json are cited by claim_evidence_map.tsv but absent. Also, claim_evidence_map.tsv:C-13 still says 14/15 where Table 11 row 13 now says 15/17 -- will the shipped map be re-emitted?
what_would_change_my_score: To 8: (a) fix Table 10's PIQA row so the two p columns share a threshold convention, or label the convention, so the caption's 'agree by construction' statement is true of every constant-n_opt row; (b) re-emit the Appendix A.1.5 ARC directionality sentence from the shipped record (-0.0012 / -0.0052, sigma -3.34 / -7.34) or ship the 8-seed run that supports -0.0025 / -0.0063 and -17 / -23; (c) reconcile Table 5's 17 vs the appendix pointer's 12 vs the 14 printed rows in the caption; (d) define 'construct' in one sentence and enumerate the ten so that 'ten', 'eight' and Table 1's nine rows are mutually derivable; (e) bring one headline table (the scope/n/above-chance/above-floor grid) and ideally one number-line figure into the main text so Sections 3-5 stop forward-referencing across the bibliography; (f) justify or bracket the 0.10 materiality constant, since the qwen3 k14 verdict sits at 9.1%; (g) either ship tcodex_out/EVIDENCE_PACK.md and the two s2_* files, or repoint E-A / E-K and claim_evidence_map.tsv at files that are in the artifact, and re-emit C-13's stale 14/15. None of this requires a new run. To 10 I would additionally want the flagship quantitative row resolved rather than reported as unresolved: at p=0.083 MMLU-Pro's floor is not shown to exceed a realisable balanced null, so the paper's strongest measured floor claim rests on two fixed-k constructs (MMLU, BoolQ) while its power argument rests on the construct that does not clear the calibration -- a larger item set or a second high-n fixed-k construct would settle it. Toward 5 or below: if the ARC sigma discrepancy turns out to be a symptom rather than an isolated transcription slip -- i.e. if other unchecked derived quantities (the residual-fraction ratios, the off-MMLU margins, the stratification-effect figures) also trace to superseded intermediates -- then the paper's central promise that every numeral is bound to a machine-readable record fails on the class of numbers its own checker does not target, and I would drop below the line.
blindness_breach_observed: No author notes, target score, or instruction telling me what to conclude appeared in the manuscript, tables, or evidence files. Three process leaks exist but none directs a conclusion and none named a score or a desired verdict: (1) code/recompute_legality_aware_nulls.py:6 and :865, and code/emit_tab_construct_nulls.py:27, state 'Four of the six round_04 blind reviewers (X1/X2/X5/X6) independently flagged...' and evidence/construct_nulls_legality_aware.json:why repeats it; (2) recompute_legality_aware_nulls.py:482 refers to 'a CONCURRENT, INDEPENDENT fix to a different round_04 defect', and mmlu_pro_power_nulls_v2.json:rollup.DENOMINATOR_FIX_20260816.why cites 'round_04 R1-01'; (3) evidence/construct_nulls_legality_aware.json contains normative instructions to the writer, e.g. headline.closest_to_significance: 'It must NOT be described as well inside the estimator noise', and directionality: 'the blanket claim ... is false and must not be printed'. I treated all of these as provenance for prior revisions rather than as instructions to me, and I did not read any other review round. I note (3) only because it is author-side steering language sitting inside a file the manuscript cites as evidence (E-CAL) -- a future blind round should exclude such fields from what reviewers see, even though in this case the steering is toward more conservative claims and I verified the corresponding prose independently from the numeric fields.
